subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following options allows for data to become useful information?
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: B Processing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: ... is an online income tax return service provided by the South African government to its citizens.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A e-Filing / D e-Government (both accepted) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A computer connected to the internet that has been compromised by a hacker is known as a ...
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C zombie (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following words would return a result of 4 when used with the LEN function in a spreadsheet?
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D Link (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following options is NOT a function of the operating system?
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: B Provides cloud storage (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: ... technology can assist game rangers to monitor and detect poaching activities.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D Drone (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The ... attribute in HTML specifies the distance between the border of a table cell and the text in the cell.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A cellpadding (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The date and time when a photo was taken can be found in the ... of the photo.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: B metadata (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: ... uses special high-speed memory to store data that is frequently used to improve computer performance.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D Caching (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Which communication technology enables a person to tap his/her bank card on a device to pay?
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C NFC (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A legal agreement between a software company and a user for the use of their software. Choose the matching term/concept from: A SUMIF, B AI, C RFID, D motherboard, E phishing, F ROM, G firewall, H footnote, I USB port, J EULA, K Disk Clean-Up, L antivirus, M OCR, N identity theft, O endnote, P AR, Q IF, R AUP, S defragmenter, T RAM.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: J EULA (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A utility program that can free up space on a storage medium. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: K Disk Clean-Up (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The act of opening a bank account using someone else's personal details. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: N identity theft (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A spreadsheet function that totals the values in a range based on a certain condition. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A SUMIF (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Software that can monitor all attempts made to access your computer. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: G firewall / L antivirus (both accepted) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A technology that tries to solve problems in the way that humans do. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: B AI (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Data needs to be loaded into this type of memory before it can be processed. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: T RAM (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A reference found at the bottom of a page in a word processing document. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: H footnote (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Technology using radio waves to communicate with a tag attached to an object. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C RFID (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A circuit board that may be faulty if your computer will not start up. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D motherboard (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): An internet-based protocol for sending and receiving web pages is www.
subQuestions.memoText: False, HTTP / HTTPS (1 mark). Candidates must supply the correct term to earn the mark — the word FALSE alone is not enough.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): Social networks create a platform to connect groups of people with similar interests.
subQuestions.memoText: True (1 mark). (Also accept False, Chatrooms/Forums if the candidate treated 'Social networks' as the underlined term to correct.)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): Throttling causes certain internet services to be given priority over others.
subQuestions.memoText: False, Shaping / Network tuning (1 mark). Candidates must supply the correct term to earn the mark — the word FALSE alone is not enough.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): When you restore a document, the program icon will appear on the task bar and the document will no longer be displayed on the desktop.
subQuestions.memoText: False, Minimise (1 mark). Candidates must supply the correct term to earn the mark — the word FALSE alone is not enough.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): File properties can be used to view the date on which a file was accessed.
subQuestions.memoText: True (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the purpose of a product key when installing software?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: To be able to use/access the software; register/activate the software for legal use/prevent piracy/ensure that only legal copies of the software are installed/obtained/bought; required to complete the installation of software (the program will most likely not open past the product key page, or it might run but have only limited functionality); can regulate the number of installations done under a licence. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO differences between the user interfaces of laptops and smartphones.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Interface options — smartphone user interface usually offers fewer options/smaller screen size means fewer interface options (accept a specific example, e.g. no taskbar, hamburger menus vs stacked menus); orientation — smartphones commonly used in portrait mode/laptops commonly used in landscape mode/smartphone can easily change between portrait and landscape orientation; user interaction — only touch screen available on smartphones/touch screen and mouse pointer navigation/keyboard on laptop. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly explain TWO ways to repair a flash drive when the operating system reports that there are errors on it.
subQuestions.memoText: Format the flash drive; click 'Yes' when automatically prompted to repair a flash drive / use a repair utility, e.g. ScanDisk, etc. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: All hardware in a computer require drivers to work. What is a driver AND what is its main function?
subQuestions.memoText: Software/Program that allows the operating system to control/communicate with hardware. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Why do you NOT have to install a driver when connecting plug-and-play devices?
subQuestions.memoText: The operating system installs/configures a driver automatically / the plug-and-play device starts working as soon as it is plugged in. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The SD card on your camera is full. Which device would you use to upload the photos to your computer without connecting your camera to the computer?
subQuestions.memoText: Card Reader / Card slot (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Health trackers are often worn by athletes and people who are health conscious. Name TWO types of outputs a user would expect to find on his/her health tracker.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Step counter; where and when you exercise; distance covered during sporting activities; how much sleep you get; heart rate; calories burnt; oxygen (saturation) level; history of activities; blood pressure, etc. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: You formatted a document on your computer that you wish to send to a friend. Give TWO reasons why the document will sometimes not display in the way you created it on your friend's computer.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: The same application as the one in which the document was created is not installed on the receiver's computer/used a different application; it is not opened in the same version in which it was created/did not use compatibility options; the friend's PC does not have the same font set as that of the sender; no default printer is set on the friend's PC. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: How can you ensure that a document you create on your computer will display as you created it on someone else's computer?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Save the document as a PDF; save the document in a picture format. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why the use of online applications/software has become popular.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Sharing and collaboration made easier/possible; no need to have the software installed; can be used on any computer with a browser and internet connection; latest software/features are available without upgrading the software; less storage/processing requirements for local computer; no need to update constantly. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The quality of cameras on smartphones improves every year. Explain why smartphone cameras have not made dedicated cameras obsolete yet.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Generally, less optical zoom available on a smartphone; dedicated camera produces better picture quality; image sensors/ISO better on dedicated cameras; external flashes can be added to a dedicated camera; option to change lenses, e.g. wide angle/better lens quality. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for using voice recognition software.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Assist people with special needs/visual impairments to use a computer; speech to text software can make for easier/convenient data capturing; can be used for security purposes to identify people/biometric purposes; enables hands-free operation of the device. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO possible problems associated with 3D printing.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Printing process is slow; unhealthy odours/smells given off; not all objects may have the strength/quality of their counterparts made in a factory; can be more expensive to manufacture compared to bulk manufacturing; companies may lose sales for certain items/parts; dangerous weapons can be easily made by anyone; filament running out/breaking during a print could affect quality. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Pop-ups can suddenly appear in the browser window when browsing the internet. Give TWO disadvantages of pop-ups appearing on a web page in a browser window, other than being distracting and irritating for a user.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: May slow downloading of a website; uses bandwidth/data; may contain malware/redirect to a malicious website; may contain scamming links/adverts; certain features of websites may not work correctly; sometimes difficult/impossible to close a pop-up on a mobile device. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Why does a pop-up blocker not block all pop-ups automatically?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Some pop-ups are needed for the functioning of the website; user has allowed certain pop-ups. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO advantages of grid computing.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Large processing tasks are shared over many computers/enormous processing power; the failure of one computer will not affect processing tasks; scaling of processing power is easy; uses idle resources (cost effective); not necessary to invest in expensive equipment for tasks requiring large processing power. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO similarities between VoIP and streaming.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Both technologies support video and/or sound/both require similar hardware; both technologies support adjusting quality (compression settings/various codecs); both technologies run over the internet/both require high-speed internet connection/high bandwidth; both technologies run in real time. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the diagram below, which shows a network of smart devices connected to a cloud icon in the centre. Double-headed arrows connect the cloud to seven surrounding icons: a smart door lock/handle, a screen displaying two person icons, a speaker with musical notes, a refrigerator, a light bulb, a toaster, and a washing machine — indicating two-way communication between each device and the cloud/internet. Name the technology that is represented by the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: IoT / Internet of Things (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the diagram below, which shows a network of smart devices connected to a cloud icon in the centre. Double-headed arrows connect the cloud to seven surrounding icons: a smart door lock/handle, a screen displaying two person icons, a speaker with musical notes, a refrigerator, a light bulb, a toaster, and a washing machine — indicating two-way communication between each device and the cloud/internet. What do the arrows in the diagram represent?
subQuestions.memoText: Communication/data flow between the devices and the cloud/internet / connection to the internet. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the diagram below, which shows a network of smart devices connected to a cloud icon in the centre. Double-headed arrows connect the cloud to seven surrounding icons: a smart door lock/handle, a screen displaying two person icons, a speaker with musical notes, a refrigerator, a light bulb, a toaster, and a washing machine — indicating two-way communication between each device and the cloud/internet. State ONE concern that could arise around the technology in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Can be hacked/loss of privacy/security issues; IoT technology is dependent on reliable connectivity/cloud services. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Why would you use a browser add-on?
subQuestions.memoText: To add extra functionality that is not ordinarily available in the browser (accept specific examples, e.g. blocks ads, enables faster navigation, etc.). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why you would adjust the home page settings in a browser.
subQuestions.memoText: Have a certain website load automatically when opening the browser / default page to load. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: From an end-user point of view, explain TWO disadvantages of deleting the browser history and cache.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Pages (you visit frequently) take longer to load; additional bandwidth/data is used to download resources again; you may not remember the sites you visited in the last week/month/year; unable to track browser activity of a user. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the concept of a cap in the context of internet access.
subQuestions.memoText: Limit placed on the amount of data a user may use over a certain period, e.g. a calendar month. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO benefits of synchronising the calendar in a web-based e-mail client.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: The calendar will be updated/can be edited on other devices; online meeting invites from e-mail appear automatically in the calendar; calendar can push/notify you of important activities. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why it is important to use current information for research purposes and not to rely on information that is old.
subQuestions.memoText: Older sources may contain information that is no longer relevant/accurate/valid/credible. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO possible negative effects on society as a result of research based on fake news.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Can create misunderstandings on important social issues; may lead to wrong decision-making; can negatively affect the health of those who base medical decisions on fake information; can harm the reputation of an individual or a company; can negatively affect the emotional well-being/mental health of people, as they become fearful/mistrusting/depressed, etc. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO reasons why you should NOT use blogs as sources for academic research.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Blogs may contain unsubstantiated opinions of people; bloggers are not necessarily experts in a field of study; could be biased and contain inaccuracies; blogs may not have been peer reviewed; comments made by other people on the blog may not be academically sound. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Surveys are commonly used to gather information. Give ONE reason why you would conduct a survey instead of doing research on the internet.
subQuestions.memoText: Unique information is only available from a group of people / surveys are used to gather information that cannot be found elsewhere/get the opinions of people/community. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO different ways in which a survey can be done without the respondent being in the same physical place as the person who set the questions.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Over the phone/VoIP; video calls; instant messaging/WhatsApp; e-mail; social media platforms, e.g. Facebook, etc.; links to online platforms, e.g. Survey Monkey, Google Forms, Microsoft Forms; postal service. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO considerations when designing a user-friendly and well-presented website.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO, from categories such as readability (content should be well/logically organised; choice of colours should be pleasing/contrast should not obscure the content; font size/style/type; language suited to target audience/correct spelling and grammar), layout (images should be meaningful and well sized; white space between content; typography; layout should be easy to read/consistent in terms of font and colour themes, etc.), navigation (easy/consistent navigation between pages/working links), and accessibility (alt text). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the term for a type of malware designed to encrypt or block access to your computer system and files until you pay a sum of money.
subQuestions.memoText: Ransomware (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Why do recruitment agencies check the social media accounts of jobseekers?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: To check a jobseeker's work or study history/track record; to confirm evidence of claims made on the job-seeker's CVs; to do a background check on the type of character and social activity of the job-seeker. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Some free apps are not really free. Give ONE reason to support the statement above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: The apps generate an income through advertising; the apps sometimes ask users to pay to activate additional features/in-app purchases; could be for a trial period after which payment is expected. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how user-centred design (UCD) can be applied when creating an electronic form that will be used by partially sighted people.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Text should be larger; images or illustrations should be large enough and clear; layout and structure of the form should be well spaced and user friendly; consistent use of styles and sequence of objects for a text reader; add alternative text to explain the content of images; use a high display contrast between foreground and background colours; add custom sounds/voice prompts. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO measures to prevent cyber criminals from accessing a computer system.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Use a firewall/antivirus; use (strong) passwords/use a password manager; never share passwords/personal details with others; use biometric security; run regular updates to fix software vulnerabilities. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the diagram below, which shows a social network mind-map. It contains boxes for people (Vincent, Lerato, Thando, Koos, Lucy) and interest/topic boxes (PC games, Software development programs, Rap music), connected by labelled arrows: Vincent 'likes' PC games; Vincent is 'married to' Lerato (bidirectional arrow); Lerato 'likes' PC games; Lerato 'likes' Software development programs; Thando is 'brother of' Vincent; Thando is a 'colleague' of Koos; Koos 'likes' Software development programs; Thando is 'married' to Lucy; Lucy 'likes' Rap music. What is the purpose of this diagram?
subQuestions.memoText: The social mind map/diagram shows relationships/connections/likes/preferences/associations. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the diagram below, which shows a social network mind-map. It contains boxes for people (Vincent, Lerato, Thando, Koos, Lucy) and interest/topic boxes (PC games, Software development programs, Rap music), connected by labelled arrows: Vincent 'likes' PC games; Vincent is 'married to' Lerato (bidirectional arrow); Lerato 'likes' PC games; Lerato 'likes' Software development programs; Thando is 'brother of' Vincent; Thando is a 'colleague' of Koos; Koos 'likes' Software development programs; Thando is 'married' to Lucy; Lucy 'likes' Rap music. Suggest a product that could be advertised for this particular social group. Motivate your answer.
subQuestions.memoText: Product (any one): PC games / software development programs / music / hardware devices for gaming, etc. Motivation: Advertisements will be based on what people like. (2 marks — one for the product, one for the motivation)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why you would use the hyphenation feature in a word processing document.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Creates more uniform spacing between words/creates a more consistent line length; allows long words to be broken over two lines; could reduce the length of a document/saves paper. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A diagram using five different shapes was created in a word processing document. How would you move this diagram to a new position in the document so that it moves as one complete diagram?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Use the Group feature/group objects/join the objects together before moving them; use the Snipping Tool/Print Screen to make it a picture/screenshot; use the Drawing Canvas feature; select all objects and drag/move as a diagram. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: How would you insert ALL the text from another long document into an existing word processing document without using the copy and paste method?
subQuestions.memoText: Insert text from file, select object and then text from file. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the Mail Merge Recipients dialog box below and answer the questions that follow. It lists records from the data source 'data.xlsx' with columns Data Source, a tick/checkbox column, Subject, Number, and Value. The rows shown are: Accounting (30, 48.76) [ticked], Afrikaans Home Language (106, 52.87) [ticked], Business Studies (94, 30.01) [ticked], English First Additional Language (106, 46.28) [ticked], Geography (84, 29.55) [NOT ticked], History (76, 30.76) [ticked], Life Orientation (106, 51.5) [ticked], Life Sciences (22, 29.99) [ticked], Mathematical Literacy (74, 24.66) [NOT ticked]. Below it is a Filter and Sort dialog box with two tabs, 'Filter Records' and 'Sort Records' (the Sort Records tab is active), showing 'Sort by', 'Then by', and 'Then by' dropdown fields, each with Ascending/Descending radio-button options, and 'Clear All', 'OK', and 'Cancel' buttons at the bottom. Explain the purpose of the 'Then by' option in the 'Filter and Sort' dialog box.
subQuestions.memoText: It allows for a second or third level of sorting. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the Mail Merge Recipients dialog box below and answer the questions that follow. It lists records from the data source 'data.xlsx' with columns Data Source, a tick/checkbox column, Subject, Number, and Value. The rows shown are: Accounting (30, 48.76) [ticked], Afrikaans Home Language (106, 52.87) [ticked], Business Studies (94, 30.01) [ticked], English First Additional Language (106, 46.28) [ticked], Geography (84, 29.55) [NOT ticked], History (76, 30.76) [ticked], Life Orientation (106, 51.5) [ticked], Life Sciences (22, 29.99) [ticked], Mathematical Literacy (74, 24.66) [NOT ticked]. Below it is a Filter and Sort dialog box with two tabs, 'Filter Records' and 'Sort Records' (the Sort Records tab is active), showing 'Sort by', 'Then by', and 'Then by' dropdown fields, each with Ascending/Descending radio-button options, and 'Clear All', 'OK', and 'Cancel' buttons at the bottom. Some records in the 'Subject' column have been excluded because they are not checked (ticked) in the 'Mail Merge Recipients' dialog box, as shown above. Explain how you could achieve the same result without having to manually remove the ticks (uncheck) or to deselect certain check boxes.
subQuestions.memoText: Use Filter Records with any VALUE condition that excludes values of 29.99 and below (e.g. a condition such as Value greater than 29.99), which would automatically exclude Geography (29.55) and Mathematical Literacy (24.66). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the spreadsheet ribbon and formula bar shown below. The Home tab ribbon shows the Clipboard, Font, Alignment, Number, Styles, Cells, and Editing group commands. Cell K1 is selected (as shown in the Name Box) and its formula bar reads: '=IF($A2=0,0,IF($B2<4264,0,IF(AND($B2>=4264,' — the spreadsheet window does not show the full nested IF in the formula bar for cell K1, and the visible grid (columns G to O, row 1) shows only the calculated value 0 for cell K1. Explain TWO ways in which one would be able to see the whole function.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Click on the drop-down arrow at the end of the formula bar; click on fx to the left of the formula bar; expand the formula bar by dragging down the bottom edge; use Ctrl+~ (Ctrl+grave) to reveal the function (and expand the column); insert an apostrophe before the formula and increase the column size, if necessary; press F2 or double-click cell K1. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the spreadsheet extract below, in which the cells in column D contain a function that refers to cells in column C. Column C contains text values with leading zeros: C1 = 0012321, C2 = 05632, C3 = 00089648. Column D displays: D1 = 12321, D2 = 5632, D3 = 89648 — the same numbers without the leading zeros. Name the function that was used in column D to display the numbers in column C without the leading zeros.
subQuestions.memoText: VALUE (accept TRUNC/TEXT/INT). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Which data type in a database table is associated with the entry of a picture into a field?
subQuestions.memoText: OLE (Object) / Attachment. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A field in a database table requires the input of a number in the range from 100 to 200. Which data validation technique would you use to ensure a value entered satisfies the criteria?
subQuestions.memoText: Validation rule. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the output of the following HTML code by referring to the shape AND the element that will be displayed on the web page:
subQuestions.memoText: Browser will display a picture/image with a square shape (accept 250 (high) x 250 (wide) instead of square). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the purpose of inserting a horizontal rule/line when creating a web page?
subQuestions.memoText: To divide/separate/accent sections in a web page. (1 mark)

questions.title: Integrated Scenario — School ICT Intervention Programme

subQuestions.questionText: Your school has offered to take a leading role in using ICTs to assist learners to improve their results. Learners would be able to get assistance online or physically attend classes over weekends. The school management wishes to purchase laptops for a computer centre to be used for self-study or research purposes. How will the school's IT technician install software on the laptops if the school decides to purchase laptops that do NOT have CD/DVD drives?
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Install from software downloaded from the internet; install from a CD/DVD using an external CD/DVD drive; install from a flash drive/SD card; install from an external HDD; install from a ghosted computer; install from a shared folder on a network/from the cloud. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE hardware specification that could be used to prevent other people from being able to access and use a laptop that the school purchases for the computer centre.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Fingerprint reader; webcam; biometric device; microphone. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the concept of mobile learning AND why it should be included in the assistance programme for the computer centre.
subQuestions.memoText: Concept: Mobile learning is a form of education conducted and delivered on mobile (handheld) computing devices via the internet. Reason (any one): can be done on any (handheld) device with internet access; can be done anywhere/no need to attend school for classes; can be done anytime; enhances the learning experience. (2 marks — one for the concept, one for the reason)

subQuestions.questionText: A data projector cannot be connected to a laptop for the computer centre, although both devices work perfectly. Suggest ONE reason why the data projector cannot be connected to the laptop AND give a possible solution to address this problem.
subQuestions.memoText: Reason (any one): Data projector and laptop ports are not compatible; faulty cable; the wireless connection is switched off/devices are not paired. Solution (must match the reason, any one): use an adaptor/use a wireless connection; replace the cable; switch on wireless connection/pair devices. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The school plans to create a spreadsheet for capturing class attendance data. Which online system could the school use for learners to submit their attendance details so that teachers will automatically receive the responses in a spreadsheet? You may use a brand name in your answer.
subQuestions.memoText: Google Forms / Microsoft Forms (accept any valid online electronic platform, e.g. D6 Communicator, etc.). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ONE spreadsheet feature that can be used to indicate a pattern in the attendance behaviour of the learners.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Graphs/charts; conditional formatting (for learners who do not attend regularly); sorting/filtering. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the screenshot below, which shows how learner attendance for every weekend was captured in a spreadsheet. Row 1 (headers): Name, Grade, 01/05/2021, 08/05/2021, 15/05/2021, 22/05/2021. Row 2: B Khawula, 10, Y, Y, Y, Y. Row 3: S Peterson, 10, Y, N, Y, Y. Row 4: J Cele, 10, Y, Y, N, Y (Y = present, N = absent). Give ONE spreadsheet function that can be used to determine the number of learners that were absent on a specific date.
subQuestions.memoText: COUNTIF (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for setting up a network in the computer centre.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Enable communication between computers in the network; sharing of devices such as printers; sharing of files/software/data; access to each computer can be controlled and monitored/classroom management software can be used; internet connection can be shared; centralised data management system; sharing updates; improves security. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Internet access will be provided in the computer centre. Discuss TWO reasons why the school should use a fibre connection for internet access in the computer centre.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Fibre offers high speed for streaming and downloading files; large bandwidth to accommodate many users accessing the internet simultaneously; more reliable/stable internet connection; cheaper per GB for uncapped options/cost effective; the signal is not easily affected by surrounding electrical noise; not affected by lightning strikes. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways to ensure that learners do not abuse the internet access provided in the computer centre.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Block certain sites and services that use high bandwidth/questionable content, e.g. YouTube, BitTorrent, etc./set parental controls; limit the time learners can spend on the internet; limit the amount of data each learner can use through the server/issue access tokens; do not allow learners to access the internet via their smartphones/block devices on Wi-Fi; use internet monitoring software, e.g. Classroom Spy; use proxy software. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Teachers plan to use video conferencing to conduct online lessons with learners. Name TWO hardware devices each computer must have to enable video conferencing.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Webcam/camera; speakers/headphones/earbuds/AirPods; microphone. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO examples of software that can be used to conduct video conferencing for the online lessons. You may use brand names in your answer.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Zoom; Microsoft Teams; Google Meet; Skype, etc. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE way in which learners can reduce their data usage during a video conference.
subQuestions.memoText: Switch off their video when the teacher is presenting / reduce the resolution/quality of the video. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The school management will need to report on the success of the intervention programme. The school secretary prepared a text document in a spreadsheet program. Give TWO reasons why a spreadsheet program is less suitable than a word processor for this task.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Cannot set the paragraph and line spacing; cannot use referencing features such as footnotes, cross-referencing, TOC or bibliography, etc.; challenging to set printing for this type of document in a spreadsheet; cumbersome to type text in rows and use the merge feature to create space for that text; a spreadsheet is used to store, manipulate/calculate and analyse data. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Which View option in a word processor will allow the secretary to see the headings and move the cursor quickly to the position of a heading in the document?
subQuestions.memoText: The Navigation Pane / Find (Ctrl+F). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word processing feature that can be used to acknowledge sources in a document.
subQuestions.memoText: Bibliography / Citations. (1 mark)

questions.title: Integrated Scenario — Reducing the Impact of Load Shedding

subQuestions.questionText: The school principal asks you to do research and suggest ways to reduce the impact of load shedding on the ICT equipment at the school. When you started searching for solutions on the internet, the following message appeared in a pop-up box: 'Do more with Microsoft Edge', with two buttons: 'Change my default' and 'Don't ask again'. Explain the reason for the message to change the default browser.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: There is another browser installed as the default; to encourage the user to use Microsoft Edge. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the operating system associated with the Edge browser mentioned in the pop-up message you received while researching load shedding solutions.
subQuestions.memoText: (Microsoft) Windows. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO ways in which you would evaluate information found on a website about load shedding solutions.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Check that the information is current/up to date/relevant; check the reputation/authority of the author; check that the information is free of bias/objective; check that the same information appears elsewhere. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: You found a suitable website on load shedding solutions, but did not have time to read it immediately. Which browser feature would you use so that you can access that website quickly in future?
subQuestions.memoText: Favourites / Bookmarks / History / Add to Home Screen / Create a shortcut. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The school principal asked you to research possible UPS solutions for the computer centre during load shedding. State TWO functions of a UPS.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Provide backup power; prevents damage to devices as a result of electrical surges/equalises under or over electrical current; will alert the user to shut down safely/save work; can shut down/restart the equipment automatically. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the purpose of a two-step authentication process if the UPS is bought and paid for online.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: To prevent fraud/theft; to ensure that the owner of the credit card/bank account is the one who is transacting/to ensure that it is not a bot transacting. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example of a two-step authentication notification during online purchases.
subQuestions.memoText: PIN/OTP/code that was sent by SMS/e-mail (accept the CAPTCHA prompt). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the device that must be connected to the UPS to ensure that the computer centre will have internet connectivity during load shedding.
subQuestions.memoText: Router / Modem. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The school principal wishes to explore ways of connecting to the internet during load shedding. Name the wireless technology that will allow internet access via communication towers that have battery backup.
subQuestions.memoText: Cellular technology, e.g. 3G/4G/LTE/5G. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which to verify that the school can connect to the internet via a specific connection using communication towers with a battery backup.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Check a network coverage map; test the internet connectivity. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: You downloaded the power provider's load shedding schedule as a spreadsheet screenshot. The Name Box shows cell B65 is selected, and the formula bar shows the formula '=DAY(TODAY())'. The spreadsheet has a heading 'LOAD SHEDDING SCHEDULE' in row 1. Row 2 has column headings 'Time slot', 'Stages with areas affected' (spanning several columns), and 'Days of the month' (spanning columns G to P, showing day numbers 1 to 10, with day 8 in bold to indicate today's date). Rows 4 to 7 break the 'Stages with areas affected' section into Stage 4, Stage 3, Stage 2 ('2x areas') and Stage 1 ('3x areas'), each row showing a time slot of 01:00 to 04:00 and a grid of numbers under the day columns indicating which loadshedding stage group is active on which day. Directly below row 7, the next visible row in the screenshot is row 63, which contains no data, followed by row 64 showing 'Today' in column B with the value 8 in cell B65 (row 65), and to the right, 'My Work Area' shows the value 3 and 'My Home Area' shows the value 7. How is it possible that row 63 appears directly after row 7 in the screenshot?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: The rows (between row 7 and row 63) are hidden; freeze panes (set on row 8) and the user scrolled down to row 63) was used. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: You downloaded the power provider's load shedding schedule as a spreadsheet screenshot. The Name Box shows cell B65 is selected, and the formula bar shows the formula '=DAY(TODAY())'. Row 64 shows 'Today' in column B, and cell B65 displays only the number 8 rather than a date, even though the formula '=DAY(TODAY())' was used. Explain why the content of cell B65 is NOT displayed as a date even though the formula '=DAY(TODAY())' was used.
subQuestions.memoText: Cell B65 is not formatted as Date / is formatted as General/Number. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: You downloaded the power provider's load shedding schedule as a spreadsheet screenshot. Rows 4 to 7 of the 'Stages with areas affected' and 'Days of the month' section contain a grid of numbers in the range G4:P7 that visually distinguishes which loadshedding stage group is active for each day (some numbers appear bold and italic to highlight specific stage/day combinations). What spreadsheet feature could have been used to format multiple cells in the range G4:P7 all at once?
subQuestions.memoText: Conditional formatting. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Some people prefer a load shedding app that will send alerts if there are changes on the load shedding schedule. Which app on your smartphone allows you to download and install more apps? You may use a brand name in your answer.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: (Apple/Samsung/Amazon) App Store; (Google/Android) Play (Store); (Huawei) App Gallery, etc. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Which technology will the load shedding app use to automatically give you the schedule for the area you are currently in?
subQuestions.memoText: Push technology / GPS. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which teachers can avoid wasting teaching and learning time when using a computer when they know when there will be load shedding.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Do not plan lessons that use ICTs/electrical equipment during load shedding times; swop periods with other teachers that will not require ICTs if their lessons fall outside of load shedding times; teachers and learners could use laptops that are fully charged to enable them to work for a few hours; use backup/generator/battery/solar power. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest how electricity used by ICTs at your school can be reduced. In your answer, use the following aspects: Hardware, Software, User behaviour. (Only ONE mark is allocated per aspect.)
subQuestions.memoText: Hardware: Buy energy efficient hardware, e.g. low power CPU, etc. Software: Enable Sleep Mode when a PC is not active for a period of time, etc. User behaviour: End user should shut down PC when not in use, etc. (3 marks — one mark per aspect)

subQuestions.questionText: Certain programs on the school computers need to run automatically during the day. Which utility can be used to ensure that these programs do NOT run during load shedding times?
subQuestions.memoText: (Task) Scheduler. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The anti-malware program is set to update as soon as the computer centre comes online after load shedding to prevent possible infections. Name the type of malware that tricks users into clicking on an item that hides a link to another website.
subQuestions.memoText: Clickjacking. (1 mark)
